  -- FAIL (2) --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  x port 443 answers on the raw IP 203.0.113.10 (https 404): ingress is tunnel, so this is an origin
    bypass (see CF-005)
    PRB-002, high, port:tcp/443
    rule: Web ports do not answer on the raw IP behind a tunnel
    fix:  Publish the proxy on 127.0.0.1 only and let the tunnel connector reach it locally, then
          drop the public 80 and 443 rules in the provider firewall.

  x port 6379 (Redis) answers from outside on 203.0.113.10
    PRB-005, high, port:tcp/6379
    rule: Databases are not reachable from the internet
    fix:  Turn off public publishing of the database (or publish it on 127.0.0.1), and reach it over
          the tailnet or an SSH tunnel.

  -- WARN (2) --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  ! SSH answers from outside on port 22 at 203.0.113.10 (SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_9.6p1 Ubuntu-3ubuntu13),
    although ingress is tunnel
    PRB-001, moderate, port:tcp/22
    rule: SSH is not reachable from the internet on a private ingress host
    fix:  Make SSH work over the tailnet first, then close the public SSH rule in the host firewall
          and the provider firewall (see SSH and NET checks).

  ! https://app.example.com/: redirect loop (often an app redirecting to HTTPS behind a tunnel that
    already terminates TLS)
    PRB-006, moderate
    rule: The app hostname answers over HTTPS without TLS or redirect anomalies
    fix:  Behind a tunnel, turn off the app's own redirect to HTTPS (or trust the proxy's
          X-Forwarded-Proto) and let the tunnel enforce HTTPS; renew or fix the certificate when
          verification fails.
